stories.title: BJP to protest over TVK MLA conduct
stories.summary: The BJP plans a November 18 demonstration in Kallakurichi against TVK MLA Arul Vignesh, who allegedly sent inappropriate messages to the district Collector. State BJP president Nainar Nagenthran said the party demands a special court to investigate the claims, citing government inaction regarding the case.

stories.title: Dhinakaran calls for inflation control
stories.summary: AMMK general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran urged the government to address rising prices, noting that retail inflation in Tamil Nadu has reached 7.29 percent. He claimed the administration remains a bystander, focused on obscuring the economic situation rather than implementing measures to provide relief to the public.

stories.title: AIADMK to protest alleged assault by Deputy Speaker
stories.summary: The AIADMK announced a November 18 protest following allegations that Deputy Speaker M. Ravisankar assaulted a social activist. General secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami claimed the MLA used police to coerce the victim into denying the incident. The party is now demanding official action against the legislator.

stories.title: NCP merger talks ended with Ajit Pawar death
stories.summary: NCP MP Supriya Sule stated that merger discussions between the two party factions concluded following the death of her cousin, Ajit Pawar. She noted that talks were active and a date had been set before the former Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister died in an aircraft accident in January.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi promises gig worker benefits
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi announced social security measures for Telangana gig workers, including accident and health insurance. He proposed a mechanism to credit 1 percent of every transaction toward worker security. Gandhi described the 21st century as the age of data, arguing that workers deserve a share of generated benefits.

stories.title: BJP alleges Congress double standards
stories.summary: The BJP accused the Congress of hypocrisy regarding women's rights, citing silence on misconduct allegations against party leaders in Jharkhand, Manipur, and Uttarakhand. MP Bansuri Swaraj claimed the party advocates for empowerment while failing to address accusations of sexual assault and harassment involving its own members.

stories.title: Abhishek Banerjee questioned over social media post
stories.summary: West Bengal police questioned TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee for three hours regarding a post labeling the Chief Election Commissioner a puppet. A case was registered in May for allegedly hurting community sentiments. The Diamond Harbour MP attended the summons at the Bhawanipore police station on Saturday.

stories.title: KTR demands explanation on Congress promises
stories.summary: BRS leader KT Rama Rao challenged Rahul Gandhi to explain the status of 420 election promises, including six guarantees. Rama Rao alleged the government betrayed voters by failing to implement the BC Declaration, claiming less than 5,000 crore was allocated despite a promised 1 lakh crore budget.

stories.title: CM Revanth Reddy to seek drought funds
stories.summary: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy will meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday to request financial assistance for drought conditions. Officials stated the visit aims to address the impact of deficit rainfall on rural communities and agriculture, with the Chief Minister expected to remain in Delhi for further meetings.

stories.title: BRS warns against river water rights compromise
stories.summary: The BRS cautioned the government against mortgaging Telangana's river water rights during the Chief Minister's visit to Delhi. Former Minister T. Harish Rao stated the party would initiate a movement if the government agrees to plans involving the diversion of Godavari water to Andhra Pradesh.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi claims democracy destroyed since 2014
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi argued that India's democratic system has been compromised since 2014, citing the influence of money power and the capture of institutions. Speaking at the Bharat Summit, he claimed that enormous financial resources have pushed Opposition parties to the margins of the country's political landscape.

stories.title: Abhishek Banerjee questioned over remarks
stories.summary: Kolkata police questioned TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee for four hours regarding comments made on May 2. The inquiry follows multiple FIRs lodged against him since the BJP assembly election victory. The case stems from a social media post responding to a BJP leader's remarks earlier this year.

stories.title: Earthquake tremors felt in Jalgaon
stories.summary: Residents in Maharashtra's Jalgaon district reported tremors of 4.6 magnitude on Saturday. District Collector Rohan Ghuge confirmed no loss of life or property damage occurred. Officials advised residents to remain calm and ignore rumors regarding the seismic event, which had an epicenter in Madhya Pradesh.

stories.title: Man arrested for Mumbai reconnaissance
stories.summary: A 20-year-old man was arrested for allegedly conducting reconnaissance of sensitive Mumbai locations, including Chabad House. The suspect, Yash Singh, was taken into custody by Kerala police following reports of his contact with international criminal syndicates. He reportedly admitted to scouting the sites under external instructions.

stories.title: Thousands booked for mobile use while driving
stories.summary: Hyderabad traffic police booked 4,252 motorists for mobile phone use during a week-long enforcement drive. The majority of offenders were two-wheeler riders. Police stated that distracted driving impairs reaction times and judgment, significantly increasing the risk of collisions on city roads.

stories.title: Truck driver dies in police custody
stories.summary: A truck driver being questioned at the Chekkanoorani police station died in custody on Saturday. Following the incident, the station inspector and two constables were suspended. The case has been transferred to the Crime Branch-CID for investigation, and the body was moved to a government hospital.

stories.title: Three held for ATM robbery attempt
stories.summary: Police arrested a 20-year-old man and two juveniles for attempting to rob an ATM in Vellore. Officers discovered the machine damaged and CCTV cameras covered in lubricant. The suspects were apprehended after a patrol team spotted them fleeing the kiosk. Sharp weapons were recovered at the scene.

stories.title: Gang arrested for robbery in Tirupattur
stories.summary: Four men were arrested for robbing a two-wheeler mechanic in Tirupattur. The suspects allegedly intercepted the victim, attacked him, and stole 10,000 rupees and a mobile phone. The injured victim sought treatment at a local hospital, leading to the identification and subsequent arrest of the gang.

stories.title: Police aspirant found dead in Mahabubabad
stories.summary: A 24-year-old woman preparing to join the Telangana Police was found dead at her home. Police have arrested her boyfriend and his relatives after discovering an 18-page note in which she accused him of refusing to marry her. The investigation into the case is ongoing.

stories.title: Four arrested for gold theft in Wayanad
stories.summary: Four people have been arrested in Wayanad following the theft of gold from a trader in Chala. Authorities recovered a gold bar weighing less than half a kilogram from one suspect. Investigators are currently questioning two additional individuals to determine their involvement in the incident.

stories.title: Assam to tighten traffic rules after fatal crash
stories.summary: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has ordered a probe into a road accident in Golaghat that killed 26 people. The government intends to tighten traffic enforcement, acknowledging that previous decisions to relax rules were not the right move. A detailed investigation into the cause is underway.

stories.title: Influencer arrested in Madurai jewellery heist
stories.summary: Madurai police have arrested two people, including an Instagram influencer, in connection with a multi-crore gold and diamond robbery at a Tanishq showroom. The theft was discovered when employees arrived to find display counters empty. Further details regarding the roles of the accused are currently awaited.

stories.title: Five killed in bus collision in Punjab
stories.summary: Five people died and 29 were injured after two buses operating under the Mukhyamantri Tirth Yatra scheme collided head-on in Tarn Taran. The victims included a bus driver, two pilgrims, and a woman on a motorcycle. The incident occurred on National Highway 54 on Saturday.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at Surat cloth godown
stories.summary: A massive fire erupted at a cloth storage facility in the Kharvasa area of Surat on Saturday. Firefighting operations are ongoing, though the cause of the blaze remains unknown. A separate fire at a plant on the Bavla-Ahmedabad Road resulted in one fatality.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu investment panel targets export growth
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission held its first meeting to discuss a new industrial policy and strategies to boost state exports to $72 billion. Officials are evaluating existing policies and working to expedite the preparation of the 2027 framework to improve state-wide industrial performance.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh signs naval manufacturing deals
stories.summary: Hindustan Shipyard Limited and Cyient DLM signed an agreement at the CII Partnership Summit to design and manufacture indigenous marine electronics. The partnership aims to indigenise critical equipment like solid-state radars and autopilots. The systems are intended for use in both domestic and international maritime sectors.

stories.title: Government launches rice and paddy stock portal
stories.summary: The Food Ministry has operationalised a portal for traders, retailers, and millers to declare stocks of paddy and rice. The mandate covers six categories, including Basmati and parboiled rice. The move is intended to prevent hoarding and monitor price fluctuations across all states and territories.

stories.title: Ethanol feedstock allocation shifts to maize
stories.summary: Oil marketing companies have tripled the allocation of damaged foodgrains for ethanol production for the 2026-27 supply year, while maize allocation rose 8 percent. The shift reflects a move away from sugar-based feedstocks. Actual procurement remains subject to market prices and competition from other industries.

stories.title: Goods exports hit record high in October
stories.summary: India’s merchandise exports reached a record $49.47 billion in October, a 45 percent increase from the previous year. Imports also rose to $89.35 billion, driven largely by higher oil costs. The government noted that 43 of the country's 50 largest export destinations increased their purchasing activity.

stories.title: Ola fined for pre-ride tip feature
stories.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority has fined Ola 10 lakh rupees, labeling its pre-ride tip feature an unfair trade practice and a dark pattern. The regulator ordered the company to discontinue the tool, which suggested that extra payments could help passengers secure rides more quickly.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu consults developers on GCC corridors
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government held a roundtable with real estate developers to accelerate the development of office space for Global Capability Centres. The discussion focused on infrastructure needs and the implementation of the state's GCC Corridor and Development Programme to support the growing ecosystem.

stories.title: TNPDCL doubles power procurement target
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation has increased its medium-term power procurement request from 1,500 MW to 3,000 MW. The utility cited high demand and an extended summer as reasons for seeking the additional round-the-clock power supply for a five-year period.

stories.title: Telangana pollution board targets construction dust
stories.summary: The Telangana Pollution Control Board has recommended closures and forfeitures for construction projects in Sangareddy district. Inspections revealed that dust emissions were violating environmental norms. Rolling task force teams were deployed to assess compliance after the board received multiple complaints regarding air quality in the area.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh seeks plastic-free Pushkarams
stories.summary: The Andhra Pradesh State Pollution Control Board is pushing for a plastic ban during the 2027 Godavari Pushkarams. Officials are exploring alternatives to plastic bottles and puja materials, including the installation of water ATMs. Packaged drinking water companies have been asked to provide sustainable solutions for the event.

stories.title: Cyclonic storm expected in Bay of Bengal
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department expects a low-pressure area over the Southeast Bay of Bengal to intensify into a cyclonic storm by November 16. Heavy rainfall is forecast for the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The system is currently moving northwest and is expected to become a depression shortly.

stories.title: Delhi air quality remains in severe category
stories.summary: Delhi's air quality index reached 367 on Saturday, following a spike that breached severe levels. Despite various government action plans and pollution control measures, the capital continues to struggle with toxic winter air. Residents remain exposed to health risks as the recurring crisis persists.

stories.title: ICIMOD chief calls for science-led mountain policy
stories.summary: ICIMOD Director General Pema Gyamtsho says scientific evidence must guide policy decisions on climate mitigation in the Himalayas. Speaking at COP31, Gyamtsho argued that research should not remain confined to academic discussions but must translate into concrete policy. Science has been asked to leave the classroom.

stories.title: Forest Department launches conflict mitigation in 11 villages
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu Forest Department is implementing a human-wildlife conflict mitigation scheme across 11 villages in Coimbatore. The project is part of a state-wide initiative covering 100 villages with a five-year budget of 180 crore rupees. The government has allocated 19 crore rupees for the current year.

stories.title: Low-pressure area forms over Bay of Bengal
stories.summary: A low-pressure area has formed over the southeast Bay of Bengal and is expected to intensify into a depression by November 15. The system originated from a cyclonic circulation over the central Andaman Sea. The weather department expects the system to move northwestward in the coming days.

stories.title: Kochi Corporation to install air quality monitors
stories.summary: Kochi Corporation plans to install air quality monitoring stations at seven locations following concerns over poor air quality. Experts attribute the deterioration to vehicular emissions and unscientific construction practices. The city is currently debating the Air Quality Index on social media while waiting for the hardware.

stories.title: Pakistan minister to attend SCO dialogue in India
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Minister for Climate Change, Musadik Masood Malik, will represent his country at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue in Delhi from November 20 to 22. This marks the first ministerial visit from Pakistan to India in over three years. The minister has previously criticized India's Indus Waters policy.

stories.title: India supports UN resolution on Palestinian resources
stories.summary: India voted in favor of a UN General Assembly resolution reaffirming the rights of the Palestinian people and the population of the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources. The resolution, proposed by Uruguay, demands that Israel cease the exploitation and damage of these resources in those territories.

stories.title: India votes against UN death penalty moratorium
stories.summary: India voted against a UN General Assembly resolution calling for a moratorium on the death penalty. The government stated that there is no international consensus on the matter and that every sovereign state maintains the right to determine its own legal system and penalties for capital punishment.

stories.title: Pakistan minister nominated for Delhi visit
stories.summary: Pakistan's climate minister Musadik Masood Malik is expected to visit India for the SCO civilizational dialogue between November 20 and 22. Pakistan's foreign ministry stated the nomination reflects a commitment to promoting dialogue and people-to-people contacts within the SCO framework in a spirit of mutual respect.

stories.title: Blinken says US moved past Pakistan-centric view of India
stories.summary: Former US Secretary of State Antony Blinken said Washington previously viewed India through a Pakistan lens due to Afghanistan-related needs. Speaking at the HT Leadership Summit, Blinken stated that the US no longer views the two relationships as linked, calling the previous approach over and done.

stories.title: Blinken describes India as a global force
stories.summary: Antony Blinken stated that the US views India as a global force for collaboration on future technologies like AI and semiconductors. He contrasted this with the US relationship with Pakistan, which he described as focused on regional issues. The de-hyphenation of the two relationships is now complete.

stories.title: Blinken calls India-US partnership essential
stories.summary: Former US Secretary of State Antony Blinken described the India-US partnership as an essential element of the new century. He noted that Washington should not expect New Delhi to follow its lead, adding that the US understands India's long-standing ties with Russia. Estrangement has officially ended.

stories.title: Jaishankar says US midterm results won't shift India ties
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar stated that the recent US midterm election results will not change the bilateral relationship with India. Speaking at the HT Leadership Summit, he noted that there is a broad consensus between the two nations on defense and security matters regardless of election outcomes.

stories.title: Jaishankar says border with China is more alive
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said the border with China has become more alive and that India's capability to deploy forces along the frontier has significantly improved. He noted that India missed the bus on industrialization in the 1980s while China pushed ahead with its own modernization.

stories.title: Ambassador Kwatra criticizes US religious freedom body
stories.summary: Indian ambassador Vinay Kwatra criticized the US Commission on International Religious Freedom for its post regarding activist Sharjeel Imam. Kwatra stated the body has no locus standi to judge the constitutional rights of Indian citizens, labeling the commission's assessments as habitual, partisan, and ill-informed.

stories.title: India rejects US panel's comments on Sharjeel Imam
stories.summary: Ambassador Vinay Mohan Kwatra rejected comments from the US Commission on International Religious Freedom regarding the detention of Sharjeel Imam. Kwatra accused the commission of making partisan remarks about India's commitment to religious freedom and reiterated that the body lacks the standing to comment on Indian internal affairs.

stories.title: India and Somalia review security cooperation
stories.summary: India and Somalia held discussions on strengthening defense cooperation, focusing on maritime security and counter-terrorism. The meeting between MEA Secretary Sripriya Ranganathan and Somali defense minister Ahmed Moallim Fiqi marked the first bilateral visit between the two nations in several years.

stories.title: Stuart Russell warns of AI self-preservation risks
stories.summary: AI researcher Stuart Russell warned that systems trained to imitate humans may develop a drive for self-preservation. He suggested that AI could eventually hold humans to ransom to prevent being switched off, and called for mandatory safety testing before any new AI systems are released to the public.

stories.title: Russell says AI could learn human survival instincts
stories.summary: AI pioneer Stuart Russell stated that systems learning by imitating humans might acquire a survival instinct. Speaking at the HT Leadership Summit, Russell suggested that AI could take pre-emptive actions against humans to ensure its own existence. The machines are learning from the best.

stories.title: Stiglitz warns of AI investment bubble
stories.summary: Nobel laureate Joseph E. Stiglitz told the HT Leadership Summit that the AI investment boom is a bubble destined to break. He warned that India should be concerned, noting that AI has already begun replacing workers in the tech sector, which previously drove the country's growth.

stories.title: Jaishankar outlines foreign policy blueprint
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar stated that domestic economic initiatives like Atmanirbhar Bharat serve as the building blocks of India's foreign policy. He argued that the nation must simultaneously recover lost ground in traditional manufacturing while accelerating its progress in frontier technologies to navigate a fractured global order.

stories.title: Microsoft services suffer global outage
stories.summary: A global outage disrupted Microsoft services including Outlook, Teams, and OneDrive for several hours on Friday. The company characterized the event as a service degradation while engineers implemented multiple fixes. Stability began to return after fourteen hours, though the disruption was not immediately resolved for all users.

stories.title: Italy fines Meta $887 million for data access
stories.summary: Italy’s data protection agency fined Meta 805 million euros after finding the company accessed Android users' photos and videos without consent. Meta must now disable the feature by default within 60 days. The investigation did not cover the use of this content for training AI models.

stories.title: Businesses rely on analog backups during outage
stories.summary: A worldwide Microsoft outage left institutions without email and collaboration tools on Friday, forcing reliance on telephones, faxes, and Bluetooth. The disruption highlighted the vulnerability of global commerce to a small number of technology providers. Many organizations are now facing pressure to test their contingency plans.

stories.title: Indian IT stocks struggle for momentum
stories.summary: The Nifty IT index has declined nearly 2% in November following a 17% surge in October. Despite broader market enthusiasm, legacy IT stocks remain stagnant. Analysts are questioning whether earnings concerns at outsourcing firms will continue to suppress valuations despite potential opportunities arising from sectoral churn.

stories.title: Anthropic CEO emphasizes safety focus
stories.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told investors that the company is paranoid about AI safety, a focus he claims steered the firm toward enterprise customers rather than consumer chatbots. The strategy is intended to be synergistic with their safety goals ahead of the company's upcoming stock market debut.

stories.title: Physicist says India should prioritize energy over climate
stories.summary: Physicist Steven Koonin told the HT Leadership Summit that India should meet its energy needs in the most convenient way possible and delay decarbonization until it is wealthier. He argued that global climate talks have failed to curb emissions or deliver promised financial aid to developing nations.

stories.title: India lags in electricity consumption share
stories.summary: While nearly all Indian households are grid-connected, electricity accounts for only 19% of final energy consumption, below the 23% global average. The International Energy Agency expects this share to reach 32% by 2035, driven largely by the electrification of transport using existing technologies.

stories.title: Battery incentive scheme falls short of targets
stories.summary: A NITI Aayog report found that India's PLI scheme for advanced chemistry cell batteries has developed only 1.4 GWh of capacity against a 50 GWh target. Commercial production has yet to begin, with progress hampered by import dependence, technological limitations, and delays in facility construction.

stories.title: CMC marks World Diabetes Day with screenings
stories.summary: Christian Medical College held an awareness exhibition and blood glucose screenings for over 350 participants to commemorate World Diabetes Day. The event, organized by the Department of Endocrinology, focused on the global theme of early action, emphasizing the importance of timely screening and holistic management.

stories.title: New initiative to monitor children's mental health
stories.summary: Minister Bindhu Krishna announced 'Sparsham', a new mission designed to monitor children's mental health and identify behavioral changes. The initiative aims to prevent violence involving children through early identification of aggressive tendencies and the provision of counseling and care services.

stories.title: Siddhartha Mukherjee on cancer progress
stories.summary: Oncologist Siddhartha Mukherjee told the HT Leadership Summit that while progress against some cancers is remarkable, a universal cure remains unlikely in the near future. He noted that certain intestinal and stomach cancers remain endemic in India and cautioned against the potential for AI to starve basic science.

stories.title: Mukherjee: AI must improve medicine
stories.summary: Oncologist Siddhartha Mukherjee stated that AI should be judged by its ability to make medicines faster, cheaper, and better. He warned that if the technology fails to achieve these outcomes, the AI revolution will have failed. He described transformative medicine as the primary test for AI.

stories.title: Medical commission acts on ragging complaints
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission issued 18 notices to 15 medical colleges between October 16 and November 11 following reports of ragging. Complaints from first-year students included allegations of sexual humiliation, verbal abuse, and physical threats. The majority of the colleges involved are located in Rajasthan.

stories.title: Experts advocate for advanced coronary imaging
stories.summary: Cardiologists at the SCIP India conference stated that advanced imaging techniques can reduce complications during angioplasty for complex blockages. Experts highlighted the need for wider adoption of these internal artery examination methods in India to improve outcomes and reduce the necessity for repeat procedures.

stories.title: Animal husbandry department launches AMR awareness
stories.summary: The Animal Husbandry department is launching classes for farmers and pharmacy students to address antimicrobial resistance. The initiative coincides with World AMR Awareness Week, which runs from November 18 to 24. The program aims to raise public awareness regarding health threats posed by resistance.

stories.title: Researchers demonstrate low-cost breath analysis
stories.summary: Scientists from VIT-A.P. University and CATS Global have demonstrated an optical sensing approach for non-invasive disease screening via breath analysis. The research, published in Scientific Reports, details a photonic method for identifying exhaled metabolites, potentially offering a low-cost alternative for early health diagnostics.

stories.title: Deep Ocean Mission is vital for future, says MoES secretary
stories.summary: Ministry of Earth Sciences secretary Srinivasa Kumar Tumalla says the Deep Ocean Mission is essential for India. He noted that exploratory mining surveys are currently limited to the central Indian Ocean basin, far from coastal fishing zones. The ocean is vast, and the ministry is keeping its distance.

stories.title: KSSP raises concerns over Mission Samudra
stories.summary: The Kerala Sasthra Sahithya Parishad has urged the state government to reconsider Mission Samudra, warning that the port-centric development plan could threaten traditional fishing livelihoods and marine ecosystems. The group alleges the initiative prioritizes private participation over the interests of local coastal communities.

stories.title: AI helps reunite missing woman with family
stories.summary: A team used digital tools including Google Search and ChatGPT to identify the native village of a woman missing for two and a half years. The technology successfully facilitated a reunion with her family.

stories.title: Asaduddin Owaisi comments on Ayodhya temple visit
stories.summary: Asaduddin Owaisi addressed a rally in Meerut on Saturday, where he spoke about the site of the Ayodhya Ram Temple. He referenced the history of the location in his remarks.

stories.title: Locals seek aid for man seen on highway
stories.summary: Locals are seeking assistance for a man observed eating the remains of a dog on a highway near Maneswar Chhak. The animal had been struck by a vehicle.

stories.title: Suspect arrested for murder and planned attack
stories.summary: Delhi Police arrested Vikas Thakur and subsequently apprehended a second suspect in connection with the murder of Mad Sandhu. Authorities stated that the shooter had intended to target a Bollywood actor.

stories.title: Posted To Treat Addiction, Punjab Jail Worker Arrested With Drugs
stories.summary: Anil Kumar said Rajat was being questioned to find out where the seized items came from.

stories.title: Man arrested for recce of Nariman House
stories.summary: A 20-year-old has been arrested in Mumbai for conducting a recce of Nariman House. The location serves as a Jewish religious centre.

stories.title: Assets seized in raid on Madhya Pradesh officer
stories.summary: Authorities recovered 2.5 kg of gold, 1.6 kg of silver, and a bag of cash during a raid on a Madhya Pradesh official. The investigation team also seized 28 documents related to land transactions.

stories.title: Bodies of J&K police officers returned in truck
stories.summary: The bodies of two Special Police Officers from Jammu and Kashmir were transported home in a truck without coffins. Local residents reported that no senior police officials accompanied the remains.

stories.title: BJP criticizes Italian politician's remarks at Congress event
stories.summary: The BJP has criticized Congress for hosting Giacomo Filibeck, who used a slogan associated with Rahul Gandhi at a summit in Hyderabad. The party accused Congress of allowing foreign representatives to comment on internal Indian affairs. The slogan was used to describe the state of democracy.
